changeability.rationale: The flagship fix (sprite) is one obvious place, but URL-name normalization and the name-fallback logic are copy-pasted per resource, so some bug classes need N edits.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:41 — await connection() cleanly opts routes into dynamic rendering; server-only data code isolated
app/src/lib/format.ts:1-57 — pure helpers shared by server and client with no imports of either

coupling.rationale: Server/client seams are excellent and components depend on narrow props, but the apiBase threading means every new page must know how sprites resolve, and HomeView bypasses the router abstraction with its own URL/history code.

evidence: app/src/lib/cards.ts:5-25 — cardsFor is designed around the app's real variation: pokemon-refs-to-species mapping, alternate-form exclusion, note via callback not flags
app/src/components/Section.tsx:1-17 and TypeBadge.tsx:3-27 — small, composable, reusable across all pages
app/src/app/pokemon/[name]/MovesSection.tsx:60,94,133-139 — the level column is special-cased in three separate places (filter, td render, default sort)
app/src/app/pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:22-26 — resource loader/metadata pattern copied per resource instead of one generic loader
abstraction_design.rationale: The core abstractions (cards, sections, format helpers, API cache) stretch well to new cases, but the per-resource page boilerplate is copy-paste and MoveTable hardcodes its cells, so similar-but-different additions grow by duplication.

findings.issue: API responses are handled as `any` throughout (pokemon, move, ability, type records); there are no domain interfaces, so shape changes and refactors are unverifiable at compile time
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the API records actually consumed (Species, Pokemon, Move, Ability, Type) in a types module and type the loader returns

findings.issue: decode/normalize + apiOrNull + notFound loader duplicated verbatim in all four resource pages (also moves:11-15, pokemon:22-26, types/[name]:18-22)
findings.suggestion: Extract one generic `getResource(resource, name)` helper and thin per-page wrappers, so a change to name normalization or 404 handling lands once

findings.issue: apiBase is threaded as a prop from every page into two client components just to build sprite URLs (5 call sites)
findings.suggestion: Resolve the sprite URL server-side when building CardData (in cards.ts or page data prep) and drop the apiBase prop from PokemonCard/HomeView

findings.issue: The home list re-implements the `<ul className="cards">` + PokemonCard markup that PokemonCardList already provides
findings.suggestion: Have page.tsx build CardData[] and render via PokemonCardList, so list-structure changes touch one component

findings.issue: The `level` column is special-cased in three places: column filtering, hardcoded <td> cells, and the default-sort branch
findings.suggestion: Render body cells from the same COLUMNS descriptor used for headers and sorting (a column-level render function), so adding/removing a column is a single edit

findings.issue: toQuery hardcodes the '/?' path prefix and goToPage re-implements Link's modifier-key handling on raw <a> with history.pushState, duplicating router concerns
findings.suggestion: Derive the path from the current location, and consider next/link or router.push/replace so navigation semantics live in one framework-provided place

findings.issue: The id→types and id→generation mappings are built inline in the home page; a second consumer would re-derive them
findings.suggestion: Move these derivations into lib/api.ts as named lookups (e.g. getTypesById, getGenerationsById)

findings.issue: IndexEntry is a 4-element positional tuple, forcing readers to decode e[1]/e[2]/e[3] at every use
findings.suggestion: Use a named object type ({ id, name, types, generation }) for self-documenting access

summary: A compact, idiomatic Next 16 app with genuinely good seams: pure format helpers, a server-only API layer with centralized base URL and caching, and a cardsFor abstraction that handles the app's one real domain subtlety (Pokémon refs vs species) in one place, so the sprite bug and card-list changes are single-file fixes. The recurring costs are per-resource boilerplate copy-pasted across four pages, pervasive `any` typing on API data, and MoveTable/HomeView duplicating markup and router logic they could share. Nothing here would make me hesitate to merge it.
